explanation: Extending one side of a triangle creates an exterior angle, and this theorem says it equals the sum of the two interior angles at the far (non-adjacent) vertices. It holds because the exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight line (they sum to 180°), while the three interior angles also sum to 180° — so the exterior angle must equal what's left after removing the adjacent interior angle, namely the other two. Dragging the interior angle at B with the slider re-shapes the triangle, and the yellow exterior angle at C tracks it exactly: ext = A + 55° at every setting, which the live readout confirms.
bullets: The dashed line extends a side to form the exterior angle at C.
Exterior angle + adjacent interior angle = 180° (straight line).
The yellow arc equals the two remote interior angles ADDED.
Change the slider: ext always equals A + 55°, never just one of them.
